about.title: Riverside Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Twenty-three people died in Riverside traffic collisions in 2025. Each number is a household in Riverside County that had to arrange a funeral, sort through paperwork, and keep going without a paycheck, a parent, or a partner. Wrongful death claims exist for exactly that gap. Under California law, a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children have the first right to bring the case; if there are none, certain dependents and heirs may step in. The claim is civil, so it moves on its own track regardless of whether prosecutors ever file charges. Recoverable losses reach beyond funeral and burial costs to the financial support the person would have provided and the love, companionship, and guidance the family no longer has. Timing matters: the deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and shorter when a public agency is involved. Whether the loss happened on I-215, along SR-91, or on Van Buren Boulevard, LawProactive can connect you at no cost with an independent attorney who handles these cases.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney you're matched with will sort out who belongs on the claim before anything is filed.

items.title: The deadline is tracked from day one
items.desc: Families generally have two years from the date of death, but that window shrinks when a city, county, or state agency may share fault. Getting connected early protects the claim.

items.title: A civil case, handled separately
items.desc: Your claim does not wait on a criminal prosecution and does not depend on one. Network attorneys pursue funeral costs, lost support, and the loss of companionship on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on SR-91 near Riverside. Does that change the deadline?
items.answer: It can. When a state highway or a city street like Van Buren Boulevard is involved, part of the claim may point toward a public entity, and California requires a government claim to be filed much sooner than the usual two years. An attorney can evaluate whether that shorter timeline applies to your situation and act on it quickly.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death lawsuit is a civil action and runs independently of any criminal case in Riverside County. Families can move forward even if charges are never filed or the criminal case ends without a conviction.

items.question: What can a wrongful death claim actually cover?
items.answer: California allows recovery for funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have contributed over their lifetime, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. What that looks like depends entirely on your family's circumstances. The independent attorney you're connected with will walk through each category with you.
